3. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Pyramid Model consists of three levels: operational level, management level, and strategic level.
4. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The operational level is responsible for day-to-day operations and includes workers, supervisors, and front-line managers.
5. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The management level is responsible for monitoring, controlling, and coordinating the activities of various departments and includes middle-level managers.
6. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The strategic level is responsible for formulating organizational strategies and policies and includes top-level managers.
7. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Pyramid Model diagram illustrates the hierarchical structure of an organization with three levels.
8. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Matrix Model represents the functional structure of an organization and includes two dimensions: the functional dimension and the organizational dimension.
9. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The functional dimension includes all functional areas of an organization such as marketing, finance, production, and human resources.
10. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The organizational dimension includes all levels of management, from top-level to front-line.
11. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Matrix Model diagram illustrates the horizontal and vertical flow of information across functional areas and management levels.
